LESSON: EARTHQUAKES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.4: Earthquakes
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Earthquakes, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: howing the distribution 1. how are earthquakes of concern to humans? 2. how should people behave in case of an earthquake?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Earthquakes together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology with assistive technology is enhanced as the learner watches/listen

to audio-visual clips on the effects of earthquakes on the environment.

● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of making connections is promoted as the learner draws or describe tactile world

maps showing the distribution of earthquake zones and displays in class.

26

Values:
● Unity: Learner displays team spirit as they brainstorm on the meaning, types and causes of earthquakes in the world

● Respect: Learner displays etiquette as they interact with a resource person on disaster preparedness and management

strategies.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner watches/listen to audio-visual clips on the effects of earthquakes on the environment

and takes notes.

● Self-Esteem: Learner draws/describes tactile world maps showing the distribution of earthquake zones.

Suggested Learning Resources

Pictures, Local and extended environment, Maps, Resource persons, Models of volcanic features, Plain papers, Manilla

papers, Clay or Plasticine, digital devices with assistive technology, Charts and marker pens, Approved textbooks and other

relevant print or braille resources, Building debris/stones/bricks, Paper Mache, Whiteboards and marker pens.

Suggested Key Skills

• Examining the classification of rocks according to mode of formation and age.

• Describing the distribution of rocks in Kenya.

• Exploring the types of movements within the earth.

• Examining the theory of Continental Drift to account for the present-day positions of continents.

• Distinguish the types of folds resulting from tectonic forces.

• Analysing the significance of folding and the resultant features.

• Investigating the causes of vulcanicity on Earth.

27

• Describing features resulting from vulcanicity in the world.

• Illustrating the distribution of earthquake zones presented in appropriate print or tactile format

in the world.

• Investigating the effects of earthquakes on the environment.
